translation_notes: prefixes: SDO->sdo, SKOS->skos, OWL->owl, RDF->rdf, PROF->prof, XSD->xsd, FOAF->foaf

Literal(x, datatype=xsd:date) kept as a Literal(...) constructor call (not rewritten to a typed-literal island "..."^^xsd:date): the value comes from METADATA.get(...), not a literal string, so a bare interpolation could not be trusted to carry the same datatype (2bis pitfall); only the XSD.date attribute access was rewritten to the xsd:date prefixed-name term.

the first two .add() calls on the same subject (rdf:type, sdo:name) were fused into one +{ s a T ; p o } block: the region is double-tagged add_isolated/add_run_shared_subject, and this is the add_run_shared_subject idiom applied to its shared-subject pair.
every remaining if-guarded .add() becomes a one-line `if cond: +{ ... }` (0.4.0 compound-statement support), one +{ } per original .add().

Credit correction (2026-11-02, corpus/403 defect 3): dropped `@prefix` for `skos:`, `owl:`, `rdf:`, `prof:`, `foaf:`, declared by the mechanical draft but never used as a term in the translated region (and not among the bindings the original sets on its graph); `rdfeval check` stays OK.
